newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House bill would expand toxics information.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House bill would expand toxics information.

text.p: Legislation was offered in the House Thursday that would give parents more information on dangerous chemicals in products for their children.
The bill, by a bi-partisan group of some 70 lawmakers, would require manufacturers to report to the Consumer Product Safety Commission on dangerous chemicals in products for children.
This would give the commission a basis for banning products that contain chemicals that may cause cancer, reproductive damage, neurological damage and other health defects, backers of the bill said.
After three years manufacturers would have to make similar reports on all products, not just those for children.
The bill would also expand a community's right-to-know program called the Toxics Release Inventory which makes companies disclose their emissions of dangerous chemicals.
With the bill, companies also would have to report on how they use, store and transport toxic chemicals, as well as how they use them in products they manufacture.
The bill would also require industries to report on very small releases of certain high-risk substances such as mercury, cadmium and lead which are not currently covered by the program.
